hood_landmark.The Strip: Bellagio's dancing fountains amid the mega-casino resorts
hood_landmark.Downtown / Fremont Street: Fremont Street Experience's giant LED canopy over vintage casinos
hood_landmark.Summerlin: Red Rock Canyon's scenic drive on the city's western edge
hood_landmark.Henderson: Lake Las Vegas waterfront resort village
hood_landmark.Chinatown (Spring Mountain): Spring Mountain Road's pan-Asian restaurant plazas anchored by Chinatown Plaza

avoid.reason: Caution off the Strip and downtown/east of Fremont St at night

hood_desc: The Strip is the iconic 4-mile boulevard of mega-resort casinos, shows, clubs and fountains, the classic base for first-time visitors, nightlife and non-stop action.
Downtown and Fremont Street offer vintage neon casinos, a covered light canopy and a cheaper, retro party atmosphere, great for budget travelers and old-school Vegas fans.
Summerlin is an affluent master-planned suburb near Red Rock Canyon with golf, upscale dining and Downtown Summerlin shopping, suited to families and quieter, resort-style stays.
Henderson is a safe, family-friendly suburb southeast of the Strip with parks, lakes and relaxed neighborhoods, appealing to travelers wanting a calm residential base.
Chinatown along Spring Mountain Road is the city's beloved Asian dining district, packed with authentic restaurants and late-night eats, perfect for foodies away from the Strip.

water.note: Tap water is treated and safe to drink, though some prefer bottled for taste.

transit.pay: For RTC buses, buy passes in the rideRTC app or at ticket machines along the Strip: US$6 for 2 hours or US$8 for 24 hours, valid on the Deuce and all buses. The Monorail is separate — singles around US$6 and day passes sold at station kiosks or lvmonorail.com. No transit card needed.
transit.hours: The Deuce runs 24/7 along the Strip; the Monorail runs from 7am until midnight-3am depending on the day.
transit.note: Transit only really covers the Strip and downtown: the Monorail runs behind the east-side casinos and the Deuce runs the Strip itself. Elsewhere, use rideshare or rent a car; free trams link several resorts (e.g. Bellagio-Aria, Mandalay Bay-Excalibur).
